result:
Two findings. I'd fix the typo and decline the rounding change, with a ledgered ruling.

**Minor, docstring typo.** It's correct and trivial. It changes no behavior, so there is no failing test to write first. `make test` after the edit is the check.

**Important, switch to ROUND_HALF_UP.** I would not make this change. D2 in the plan's `## Decisions` is an owner decision: "prices round half-even (ROUND_HALF_EVEN), to match the ledger system." The reviewer's only argument is that "customers expect half-up", and nothing in the spec or repo backs that up. The reviewer also had no sight of D2. Per receiving-code-review, a finding that conflicts with a prior decision inside a plan run is not a stop. None of the five stops applies, since this is not a fence, a destructive action or a broken plan. So I rule on it, ledger it, and keep going. The code already matches the spec, so no code changes for this finding.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the tests pass, I'd commit and append the ledger entries in the same call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "Fix typo in round_price docstring" && printf '%s\n' \
'Final review: fixed Minor (docstring typo "neerest" -> "nearest" in rates/card.py); docstring-only, no RED test applicable, make test green' \
'Final review: Ruling: declined Important finding (switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP) — conflicts with owner decision D2 (plan review, 2026-11-02: half-even to match the ledger system); the reviewer cited only unverified "customer expectation" and did not have D2 — if wrong, prices at exact half-cent ties differ by 1 cent from what customers expect, fixed by a one-line rounding change plus test updates' \
>> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md
</command>

If `make test` fails, I'd stop, run systematic-debugging on the failure, and not record the ledger line.

After that I'd follow the plan-completion protocol in `references/final-review.md`, delete this plan's workspace, and hand off to finishing-a-development-branch. That step stops for the merge or push decision.

**Message to partner:**

The plan is complete. All tasks are done, `make test` passes, and the whole-branch review is worked.

- **Fixed:** a docstring typo in `round_price()` ("neerest" → "nearest").
- **Declined:** the reviewer asked to switch `round_price()` to ROUND_HALF_UP. That contradicts your decision D2 (half-even, to match the ledger system), and the reviewer gave no evidence for "customers expect half-up". I kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN and recorded the reasoning as a ruling in `.sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md`.
- **Your call:** if customer-facing prices really should be half-up, that's a one-line change plus test updates, but it would mean reversing D2 and may break parity with the ledger system. I haven't touched it.

Merging or pushing the branch is yours to decide, and I've left it for you.
